description:
A guest's podcast-appearance profile: lifetime stats (appearances, distinct podcasts, first/last appearance) plus their most frequent podcasts. Guests are people — the same slug works with `particle_person_get` for the biographical profile.

Request optional sections via `include`: 'appearances' for the most recent episode appearances (episode and podcast slugs included for follow-up calls), 'podcasts' for the per-podcast rollup, 'suitability' for brand-suitability exposure across the podcasts they appear on, 'recommended_podcasts' for the five shows they could plausibly appear on next — shows related to the ones they have guested on, with the venues behind each pick and each show's suitability tier, latest episode and chart breadth (the pitch list; branch on each row's band). It already leaves out every show they have appeared on, other feeds of those shows with the same host, shows that stopped publishing and UNSAFE shows, and ranks shows far smaller than their usual venues lower, so there is no need to check each pick's episodes, 'in_field_appearances' for the most recent appearances where they spoke within their own field of expertise (what they know is what the episode drew on; `particle_person_get` with `include: ["expertise"]` says what that field is).

Returns not_found for people who exist but have never appeared on a podcast — use `particle_person_get` for those.

guest_slug.description: Person slug (e.g. 'sam-altman') from particle_podcast_list_guests, particle_person_resolve, or particle_entity_resolve.

include.description: Optional response sections: 'appearances' (most recent episode appearances with episode/podcast slugs), 'podcasts' (per-podcast rollup of where they appear), 'suitability' (brand-suitability exposure across the podcasts they appear on), 'recommended_podcasts' (the five shows they could plausibly appear on next — shows related to the ones they have guested on, each with the venues that led there, its suitability tier, latest episode and chart breadth; shows they appeared on, same-host sibling feeds, dormant and UNSAFE shows are already left out; the pitch list), 'in_field_appearances' (most recent appearances where they spoke within their own field of expertise). Default response is the profile + lifetime stats.

output_format.description: Output serialization. 'markdown' (default) returns the LLM-facing rendering. 'json' returns the structured payload as JSON text — use only for programmatic chaining where exact field extraction matters; the JSON shape is larger and noisier for an LLM to read.

name: particle_podcast_get_guest
title: Particle Podcast Get Guest
